document: The fixed denominator for the M5 performance and reference-workload campaigns
note: This document fixes what the two remaining measurement campaigns owe before a producer or runner is allowed to call either campaign complete. The performance and reference-workload rows intentionally share one P-003 report: running the same fixed workload twice would produce two samples, not two different obligations.

execution.matrix_rule: Every report runs exactly once at each supported matrix point.
execution.numeric_status_note: The M4 numbers are provisional hypotheses from a different host and, for P-001 and P-010, an in-memory repository. No accepted document states a binding M5 throughput or latency limit. Correctness and finite resource ceilings are gates; the reported durations, rates, and efficiency values are retained observations until release planning accepts a budget.

reports.execution_context_note: The accepted performance-plan workload table defines P-001 as the in-memory no-op tasklet lifecycle overhead measurement, independent of the PostgreSQL major. This report still runs inside the shared postgres_performance binary executed once per PostgreSQL-15/18-matrixed CI job, so it is retained once per matrix point for environmental consistency, but the scenario itself opens no PostgreSQL connection and its measurements are not a claim about database behavior.

p003.source: deterministically-generated RFC 4180 CSV with a header and three scalar columns
p003.writer: test-local enlisted PostgreSQL writer using AtomicSameResource
p003.publication_note: The campaign publishes the fixture, generator, schema, digest rule, and exact command. The test-local CSV reader is evidence workload code, not an advertised IO-FLAT-001 implementation.

p010.work_per_partition: one deterministic enlisted business write and one durable partition result

design_gate_scenario_gap.note: The M5 design gate's named campaign-scenario table names no performance or reference-workload scenario. The accepted performance plan is therefore the normative denominator for these two campaigns; this scope fixes their scenario names locally and reconciles every obligation against the plan in both directions.

out_of_scope: No binding throughput, latency, or scaling-efficiency budget is invented by this campaign.
The test-local CSV parser and writer do not promote IO-FLAT-001 or add a public component API; standard CSV components remain M6 scope.
P-002 static-versus-erased measurement remains M6 scope.
No remote worker, distributed protocol, scheduler, or additional database backend is exercised.
The campaign does not promote a ledger row or select a preview release version.
